content_metadata.description: This video explores the A320 power plant's fuel system, detailing its components, functions, and operational modes, including various engine idle and IDG cooling configurations.

qAndA.question: In the Normal Return to Tank mode, what color lines represent low-pressure fuel?
In the diagram for "No Return to Tank Mode", is the Master Switch on or off?

qAndA.answer: The IDG Cooling and the Fuel/Oil Heat Exchanger.
qAndA.question: What two components are connected to the "Oil Out" line in the "Fail-Safe Mode" diagram?

qAndA.answer: To allow the engine to accelerate rapidly from idle to go-around thrust.
qAndA.question: Why is the Approach Idle speed higher than normal idle?

qAndA.answer: During periods of high engine speed that result in high fuel flow, or when fuel tank temperature is high.
qAndA.question: Under what two specific conditions is the No Return to Tank mode activated?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This diagram shows the fuel system of the B-2500 power plant, and you can see the relationship
of the Fadec with other components of the system.
The Fadec controls the supplied fuel to the engine, through the fuel metering unit, FMU.
The fuel from the fuel tanks enters the system through a low pressure fuel shut off valve.
This valve is normally opened or closed by movement of the associated master switch.
However, it is commanded closed if the fire push button is released.
The low pressure pump moves the fuel to the integrated dry generator cooler, and through
the fuel oil heat exchanger, where the lower fuel temperature is used to cool the engine oil.
This process also exchanges sufficient heat to keep the fuel from icing.
After the fuel is filtered, it passes through the high pressure pump, where the fuel pressure
is raised to levels necessary to atomize the fuel for proper combustion.
The fuel metering unit, FMU, provides some of this high pressure fuel to operate actuators
on the components shown on the left, while the majority of the fuel is delivered through
a fuel flow meter to the combustion section of the engine.
Fuel flow information is displayed on the ECAM.
The Fadec operates three idle modes when the thrust levers are in the idle detent.
These modes are the modulated idle, approach idle, and reverse idle modes.
Modulated idle occurs on the ground when reverse is not selected, or in flight when the flaps
lever is at zero.
In the modulated mode, the idle speed depends on the demand from the bleed system and the
ambient conditions.
Approach idle occurs in flight when the flaps are not set at zero.
The approach idle speed is higher than normal idle, to allow the engine to accelerate rapidly
from idle to go around thrust.
The approach idle speed is regulated according to aircraft altitude.
The reverse idle mode is selected on the ground when the thrust lever is in the reverse idle
position.
The reverse idle speed is a slightly higher value than forward idle thrust.
IDG cooling is fully automatic, and you will rarely be aware of its operation.
Even so in the next few frames we show four diagrams, so that you can view the flow of
fuel under different conditions.
The first diagram shows the IDG cooling in the normal return to tank mode.
It operates when low pressure fuel flow is used for IDG cooling, and high pressure fuel
flow is not used.
The next diagram also shows a return to tank mode, but this mode diverts the fuel flow,
and utilizes high pressure fuel flow to boost the overall flow through the system.
This configuration is set when the IDG oil and fuel limit temperatures cannot be maintained
within limits by using the normal return to tank mode.
During periods of high engine speed that result in high fuel flow, or when fuel tank temperature
is high, the fuel is not returned to the tanks.
In this situation the no return to tank mode will operate.
This frame shows an example of high engine speed.
Notice that a closed loop results, and all fuel is delivered to the engine, and no fuel
is rooted back to the tank.
This frame shows an example of low engine speed, and high IDG oil temperature.
This is also the fail safe mode.
Notice how the high pressure fuel flows in the reverse direction through the IDG cooler
from the previous diagrams.
